searchText: I have a question about this test: `ID: EOF1V0004 check that valid EOF1 can include 0xFE, the designated "invalid opcode"` Does this mean a section can end with 0xFE? Are the rules around which opcodes a section can end on still valid and if so is there a writeup of them? quickly: a code section must "end" with one of the terminating instructions: STOP, RETURN,REVERT, INVALID, ... Not found here: https://github.com/ipsilon/eof/blob/main/spec/eof.md I don't get container test 1 here: https://github.com/ethereum/tests/blob/develop/EOFTests/efValidation/EOF1_embedded_container_.json `./eofdump eofdump --hex 0xef00010100040200010006030001001404000200008000016000e0000000ef000101000402000100010400000000800000fe` produces `invalid container size: have 50, want 52`, so the container is expected to be 52 bytes but is only 50. I get the following output when unmarshalling (and disabling the size check) it: ``` Header ----------- EOFMagic: [239 0] EOFVersion: 1 KindType: 1 TypesSize: 4 KindCode: 2 CodeSize: 1 Code 0 length: 6 KindContainer: 3 ContainerSize: 1 Container 0 length: 20 KindData: 4 DataSize: 2 Terminator: 0 ----------- Body ----------- Type 0: 00800001 Code 0: 6000e0000000 Section 0: ef000101000402000100010400000000800000fe Data: 3030 ``` Which looks a bit weird to me. The data size is 2, but since the container size is 0x14 (or 20 decimal), the data is missing from the test. There is another test (EOF_embedded_container_2) 0xef00010100040200010006030001001404000200008000016000e0000000ef000101000402000100010400000000800000feaabb Which does the correct thing in my opinion (add 2 bytes of data to the test) ``` ./eofdump eofdump --hex 0xef00010100040200010006030001001404000200008000016000e0000000ef000101000402000100010400000000800000feaabb Header ----------- EOFMagic: [239 0] EOFVersion: 1 KindType: 1 TypesSize: 4 KindCode: 2 CodeSize: 1 Code 0 length: 6 KindContainer: 3 ContainerSize: 1 Container 0 length: 20 KindData: 4 DataSize: 2 Terminator: 0 ----------- Body ----------- Type 0: 00800001 Code 0: 6000e0000000 Section 0: ef000101000402000100010400000000800000fe Data: aabb ``` ^ just as an addition, the correct test looks like this imo > the total size of not yet deployed container might be up to data_size lower than the above values due to how the data section is rewritten and resized during deployment > Maybe its this? > Terminating instructions: STOP, INVALID, RETURN, REVERT, RETURNCONTRACT, RETF, JUMPF. ? Ahh sry Yes, this is the rule that explains that test, data section is allowed to be shorter than declared Reviewing this now 👍 hey <@360491619402776577>, what's your branch for EOF? https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/29518 It's still very buggy though No worries I just want to fill the basic tests for now Ah I now see what you meant, hit a panic really fast 😅 <@403707149043105803> I've reviewed and left some comments on #518, let me know what you think 👍 Comments merged. Can we also get #517 reviewed and merged? They were written before we introduced non-returning sections and a few other minor changes. The EOF tests as merged do not reflect the mega-eof EIPs without these changes.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
I have a question about this test: `ID: EOF1V0004 check that valid EOF1 can include 0xFE, the designated "invalid opcode"`
Does this mean a section can end with 0xFE?
Are the rules around which opcodes a section can end on still valid and if so is there a writeup of them?

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: quickly: a code section must "end" with one of the terminating instructions: STOP, RETURN,REVERT, INVALID, ...

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
I don't get container test 1 here:
https://github.com/ethereum/tests/blob/develop/EOFTests/efValidation/EOF1_embedded_container_.json

`./eofdump eofdump --hex 0xef00010100040200010006030001001404000200008000016000e0000000ef000101000402000100010400000000800000fe`
produces `invalid container size: have 50, want 52`, so the container is expected to be 52 bytes but is only 50.

I get the following output when unmarshalling (and disabling the size check) it:
```
Header
-----------
EOFMagic: [239 0]
EOFVersion: 1
KindType: 1
TypesSize: 4
KindCode: 2
CodeSize: 1
Code 0 length: 6
KindContainer: 3
ContainerSize: 1
Container 0 length: 20
KindData: 4
DataSize: 2
Terminator: 0
-----------
Body
-----------
Type 0: 00800001
Code 0: 6000e0000000
Section 0: ef000101000402000100010400000000800000fe
Data: 3030
```

Which looks a bit weird to me. The data size is 2, but since the container size is 0x14 (or 20 decimal), the data is missing from the test.

There is another test (EOF_embedded_container_2) 0xef00010100040200010006030001001404000200008000016000e0000000ef000101000402000100010400000000800000feaabb
Which does the correct thing in my opinion (add 2 bytes of data to the test)
